source.title: You don't need error nodes, you need better features

record.tranche_reason: The post measures how SAE training choices, encoder tuning, and encoder architecture affect reconstruction error and full-replacement-model divergence. These results bear on whether replacement error is sensitive to SAE training, but it does not reproduce the original error-vector linear-predictability or cross-size token-overlap measurements.
record.gate_note: The post reports results for SAE replacements, model divergence, reconstruction error, and error-compounding estimates. It does not report linear prediction of the error vector, per-token error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, overlap of failing tokens across sizes, comparison with equal-size random errors, or a direct test of whether error nodes preserve behavior. Those parts are not treated as measured results here.
record.test_reason: The post argues error nodes are unnecessary and measures Gemma-2-2B full replacement models without them. Even the best setup leaves a clear deficit: CE 0.76 vs 0.39 base, and MMLU below chance without fine-tuning. That bears on V5. The large changes in replacement KL across training, encoder and tuning choices bear on V6, as does single-layer error rising under these methods. It does not measure linear predictability, cross-size scaling, random-error baselines or the error decomposition, so V1–V4 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right but omits the central thesis: error nodes are fundamentally flawed for causal interventions and single-layer reconstruction is the wrong optimisation target. On that thesis, the author holds that SAEs robust to upstream error can replace error nodes, demonstrated as an existence proof with substantial remaining degradation.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains replacement-aware SAEs and tests full replacement models rather than measuring linear predictability or shared token-level errors across SAE sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Replacement-model KL and error compounding vary with replacement-aware versus standard training, KL fine-tuning, encoder tuning, and vanilla versus LISTA encoders; the post also reports a reconstruction-error trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Excess error from upstream SAEs in full replacement grows roughly as the square root of depth. Its scale constant depends on the training method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction errors compound across layers in replacement models at a method-dependent rate that can be traded against single-layer error.

record.problems: One base model is tested. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results do not isolate the effect of reconstruction error from same-size random errors, and the post says full-replacement fine-tuning was less stable. Some comparisons combine training changes, encoder tuning, and encoder architecture.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. Per-layer RRE tables and benchmark outcomes were not extracted as separate rows because they do not test the claim versions' stated error-vector, cross-size-context, or error-node comparisons.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error vector from the input activation is not measured.
Per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, shared failing contexts and scaling with width are not measured; all SAEs are width 16384.
There is no comparison of SAE errors against random errors of equal norm.
There is no split of the error into linear and nonlinear components and no test of resistance to further dictionary learning.
No circuit or steering analysis is run with and without error nodes. The argument about interventions in Appendix C is theoretical.
The roles of the sparsity penalty, shrinkage and dead latents are not tested. Whether the remaining error reflects model structure is not tested, and widths are not scaled.

missing.what: Benchmark accuracy and valid-answer rates of full replacement models vs base, showing large behaviour loss without error nodes
Per-layer full-replacement RRE: replacement-aware lower than standard after about layer 9; huge outliers for Gemma Scope and standard SAEs
Excess RRE by layer and square-root fit parameters
Greedy rollouts: Gemma Scope full replacement incoherent, tuned models fluent

record.verdict_notes: The record linked r1–r11 to V3, which needs a random-error baseline the post lacks; these rows bear on V5 and V6 instead. The key V6 tension is that methods reducing the downstream impact of error increase single-layer error. Table 14 appears to contain a duplicated row (Replacement-aware vs Replacement-aware + KL). There is one model, no uncertainty estimates, and the post is not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error vector from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error vanishes with scale.

The post measures replacement-model divergence and loss after replacing activations, but does not compare reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size; its results therefore cannot establish the version's defining comparison.
No decomposition of error into a linearly predictable unlearned-feature component and a nonlinear component resistant to further dictionary learning.
No direct comparison of circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term.
The post does not establish that dark matter mostly reflects training artifacts rather than structure in model representations, and does not test end-to-end training as a general remedy.
